items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Clarence, Dick -- Clarence -- I forget the other guy.

ctx.x: (Unintelligible) The other Palmer Brothers names? Besides Clarence.

Clarence, Dick -- Clarence -- I forget the other guy. But you ask anybody about the Palmer Brothers. They'll tell you about them. They were from New York and they sang around New York. They sang with Cab's band. They did a lot of good things. In fact, they did a record with Earl. One of the first records I ever did -- in '33, I think -- with Earl -- "Rhythm Lullabye". It was real good. You know, it was some songs from the show, the Grand Terrace (unintelligible) show. Andy Razaf, he wrote them -- most of the…

You know, we had big shows. About 12 girls, and comedians, dancers. They had the whole thing. In fact, that's when Tip, Tap, and Toe first got that drum to dance on because that -- there was a dancer up there, he used to dance with a spear. Norton Naughton and Margo was a dance team, a guy and a girl. And they used to do some real nice fancy dances, you know. And they used to use that drum.
